title: The naive framing: "does it apply right now?"
text: Someone assumed flipping a plugin's enabled flag in its settings file takes effect the moment you save the file. It doesn't. Claude code has to restart first. So, when I toggle a setting, does it take effect later? The pattern lives in one file,

title: Anatomy: the file
text: .claud/pluginname.local.md in the project root. It has two parts, YAML front matter for structured settings and a markdown body for prompts and instructions. Three things read it, bash hooks, command files, and agent instructions. It's per project, user managed, and never committed to get. Four things make it work well. Design

title: Built to fail safe
text: The schema first and decide sensible defaults for when the file doesn't exist. Most users never create it. Hook should quick exit. Check the file exists. Check it's enabled. Otherwise, exit immediately. And every project needs its own git ignore entry for the file. That step is manual, not automatic. One gap worth knowing, a setting you configure in one project

title: One gap
text: Doesn't carry over to any other project. There's no plugin-wide switch. Every project keeps its own file, its own flags, its own restart. If you expected one setting to follow you everywhere, it won't. A plugin settings file works per

title: Carry-out
text: Project, not globally, and no change takes effect until Claude code restarts. Set it, save it, restart it. That's the whole contract. Your turn. Ask Claude to add configurable settings to a project,

title: Your turn
text: An enabled flag, a validation level, and a max retries count. Watch three things. First, does the file land in a per project location kept out of git? Second, does the code guard with a quick exit? Check the file exists. Check it's enabled before doing anything else.
